messages:
infra-bot: 🔔 ALERT: detect.ecc.xid_spike on cluster infer-10 (approx 12 GPUs). Error rate crossed threshold (xid 13/17). Sample log: ``
2026-03-17T18:12:14Z [gpu0] Xid 13 at nv_driver.c:452
2026-03-17T18:12:14Z [gpu1] Correctable ECC event
``

pranav: saw the alert. checking node list and kvcache usage.

sasha: oncall? this looks like the same pattern we saw in feb—hotspot on kvcache growth followed by oom and driver resets.

oncall-next: I'm on it, jumping in. starting with telemetry and health: `kubectl get pods -n infer --field-selector=status.phase=Running` and `nvidia-smi -q` on affected host.

ops-bot: runbook-link: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/gpu-xid -> recommend: cordon + migrate heavy workloads, kill stuck containers, then soft-reboot driver if needed. :link: :gear:

pranav: let's cordon node infer-10-07 and start migrating pods. I'm starting a draining with `kubectl drain infer-10-07 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --force` (will allow 30s for graceful termination).

infra-bot: telemetry spike: kernel messages show repeated `NVRM: Xid (PCI:0000:05:00): 13` on gpu0,gpu2,gpu3 within last 2m. ECC correctable rising from 0.2->4.7 per min.

lina: customer-impact check: embeddings and rerank routes are seeing elevated errors. support-jordan, can you confirm which customers hit the most?

support-jordan: listing top affected customers from 18:10-18:15: acme-inc (40 failed requests), flume-analytics (12), test-sandbox (3). No P0 escalations yet; customers on Dedicated may see degraded throughput.

sasha: toggle plan: 1) throttle embeddings route by 50% via gateway rate limit 2) fallback to smaller quantized model for open-api tenants 3) cordon & reboot nodes as prio. Any objections?

oncall-next: thumbs up. I'll apply a temporary rate-limit: `redwoodctl routes update --route /v1/embeddings --qps 50%` and spin up fallback model group `small-quant-v2` for incoming traffic.

pranav: drain progress: 8/12 pods migrated. saw one pod stuck in Terminating for 120s due to kvcache lock; executed `kubectl exec -n infer stuck-pod -- kill -9 1`.

infra-bot: driver reset initiated on infer-10-07 (soft reset). Monitoring for repeated Xid after reset window (5m).

sasha: if resets continue after soft driver reset, plan to cordon more nodes and escalate to hardware team for ECC inspection and possible GPU replacement.

ops-bot: escalation checklist posted to thread: https://redwood.internal/ops/escalation/gpu-hardware - include serial numbers, logs, and time-window.

pranav: reboot succeeded, driver reloaded. current `nvidia-smi` shows all GPUs healthy but ECC corrected counts still elevated on gpu2. Running `stress-ng --cpu 2 --timeout 30s` to validate stability.

infra-bot: post-reset telemetry: Xid events dropped to zero in last 90s, corrected ECC per-minute trending down. No kernel oops observed.

lina: customer-impact update: errors for acme-inc reduced from 40 -> 2 after throttles & fallback. I'll follow up via CS channel and open a bridge if they need live updates.

support-jordan: will message affected customers with ETA and mitigation steps; no escalations opened.

sasha: quick note for postmortem: collect kvcache metrics, driver version (nv 530.90), container logs for stuck terminations, and timeline of rate-limits/fallbacks.

oncall-next: handing off to next oncall for monitoring window. Summary: Xid/ECC spike on infer-10 cluster, cordoned infer-10-07, drained and soft-rebooted driver, temporary route throttles and model fallback applied, customer impact reduced. Please follow up with hardware ticket if ECC correctable counts don't normalize in 24h. :white_check_mark:

pranav: adding link to artifacts: s3://redwood-ops/incidents/5798765432/logs/ and trace: https://redwood.internal/traces/5798765432

ops-bot: Incident closed for paging. Monitoring phase -> watch for recurrence. :eyes:
